**CORAL** (COnsistent RAnk Logits) is a framework developed by Wenzhi Cao, Vahid Mirjalili, and Sebastian Raschka in 2020 for rank-consistent ordinal regression for neural networks with application to age estimation. The work was published in Pattern Recognition Letters, volume 140, pages 325-331, with DOI 10.1016/j.patrec.2020.11.008.

**Key aspects of CORAL:**

- It is a framework with strong theoretical guarantees for rank-monotonicity and consistent confidence scores.
- Neural networks are equipped with ordinal regression capabilities by transforming ordinal targets into binary classification subtasks; however, this method suffers from inconsistencies among the different binary classifiers.
- The proposed method is architecture-agnostic and can extend arbitrary state-of-the-art deep neural network classifiers for ordinal regression tasks.
- It was originally developed in the context of age prediction from face images and was evaluated on several face image datasets for age prediction using ResNet-34.

CORAL and CORN implementations for ordinal regression with deep neural networks are available. The work has been widely adopted, with implementations available in both PyTorch and TensorFlow/Keras.

## Key Findings on Paraphrasing and Watermark Detection:

Existing LLM-generated detectors show competitive performances in telling apart LLM-generated and human-written text, but this performance is likely to deteriorate when paraphrased texts are considered.

### Paraphrasing as an Attack Strategy

Watermarks can be easily eliminated by paraphrase and, correspondingly, the detection effectiveness will be greatly compromised. More specifically, individuals seeking to improperly utilize LLMs without being detected can paraphrase the generated contents, like altering the order and the choices of the words, and only retain the general meaning of the text to achieve their malicious goals like faking news.

Some approaches introduce iterative decoding or re-ranking to strengthen watermark robustness. While these methods improve detection under adversarial conditions, they significantly increase computational overhead, potentially degrading fluency or inflating perplexity.

### Advanced Attack Methods

Recent research has also developed more sophisticated paraphrasing attacks. A Self-Information Rewrite Attack (SIRA) leverages vulnerabilities by calculating the self-information of each token to identify potential pattern tokens and perform targeted attack. Experimental results show SIRA achieves nearly 100% attack success rates on seven recent watermarking methods with only $0.88 per million tokens cost.
